recomps.name: Transformers: War for Cybertron
recomps.tagline: Online again · FSR upscaling · built from your own disc
recomps.description: Play War for Cybertron online again on PC — no VPN, no IP addresses, no port forwarding. Built on your PC from your own USA disc, with FSR upscaling.

install.needs: WFC is built on your PC from your own disc (about 5–15 minutes). If they're missing, Hanami installs the free build tools first — CMake, Ninja, LLVM/Clang and Visual Studio Build Tools — and Windows asks you to allow each one. Needs about 25 GB free while building, about 10 GB after.

recomps.credits: Community Online Edition by Myowcha. Built with ReXGlue (BSD). AMD FidelityFX (FSR) by AMD.

builds.notes:
- Installer now loads the Visual Studio C++ build environment before compiling, so the build no longer fails at “Configuring” with missing oldnames.lib / msvcrtd.lib on some PCs
- No game changes; if you already built and play fine, nothing to do

- Installer now finds winget on its own — even when the window was opened as administrator or Windows hasn’t refreshed its PATH yet (fixes “winget is not available” on some PCs during setup)
- No game changes: your online name, settings and saves are untouched, and no rebuild is needed

- Hanami shows its own achievement popups for WFC, with gamerscore and platinums
- The game’s own "Achievement Unlocked" popup is switched off when you play from Hanami (it still shows if you start WFC another way)
- Rebuilds the game from your disc files once (a few minutes); your online name, settings and saves are kept

- Community online: lobbies, co-op, versus and escalation
- FSR upscaling presets (720p → 1440p by default)
- Built on your PC from your own USA disc

recomps.name: Dragon Ball: Raging Blast Reborn
recomps.tagline: Raging Blast 2 reborn · RB1's fighters & maps · Tag Team · rollback online
recomps.description: RB3 REBORN: Raging Blast 2 rebuilt with Raging Blast 1's characters and maps, new menus, Tag Team battles and rollback online through the same server as WFC. Built on your PC from your own Raging Blast 2 and Raging Blast 1 (USA) discs — no game files are downloaded.

install.needs: Raging Blast Reborn is built on your PC from your own discs: it needs both your Raging Blast 2 (USA) and Raging Blast 1 (USA) ISOs. Pick your Raging Blast 2 ISO here, and the installer then asks for your Raging Blast 1 (USA) ISO (Reborn uses its characters and maps). If they're missing, Hanami installs the free build tools first — CMake, Ninja, LLVM/Clang and Visual Studio Build Tools — and Windows asks you to allow each one. Building takes about 10–25 minutes and needs about 40 GB free.

recomps.credits: Dragon Ball: Raging Blast Reborn by Myowcha. Tag Team + rollback online by a friend of the project. Built with ReXGlue (BSD).

builds.notes:
- Online: smoother on long-distance connections - when the ping is 120 ms or more, the game now uses one more frame of input delay, so it has to rewind and replay far less (that replaying is what made slower PCs stutter online)
- This update compiles two changed game files again (both players need this version)
- Online (likely fix): the landing desync - when a knocked-away fighter lands, the game reads leftover scratch memory it never filled in, and that leftover was different on each PC (one tilted the fighter up, the other down). That scratch memory is now cleared before every fight step, so both PCs read the same
- Desync hunt: if it still happens, the recorder now also keeps the fighters' poses (both players need this version)
- This update compiles two changed game files again
- Desync hunt: when a match goes out of sync, each PC now also saves exactly what the landing collision checks answered in the last few seconds, plus which CPU it has (logs\online_landing_*.txt) - both players need this version
- New name: Dragon Ball: Raging Blast Reborn
- This update compiles one changed game file again
- Online: the battle's random numbers now only move with the fight itself, so they stay the same on both PCs (screens, menus and cameras use their own)
- Desync hunt: the recorder now also keeps the fight's collision checks and its effects (dust, debris, ki) and the fighters' animation state (both players need this version)
- This update compiles two changed game files again
- Fixed (online): desyncs when a knocked-away fighter lands or tumbles - the game read the ground under the fighter while another CPU thread was still working it out, so the two PCs could get different results; it now waits for that work to finish
- Fixed (online): a stage particle effect used up random numbers on only one of the two PCs
- This update compiles three changed game files again (both players need this version to play online)
- Fixed (online): the game dropped to a few frames per second during knock-aways on long-distance connections - the knock-away wait is now only used when the connection is fast enough for it
- Fixed (online): desyncs after a transformation - the transformation scene now lasts exactly the same on both PCs (it could be a few frames longer on one of them)
- This update compiles one changed game file again
- Desync hunt: the recorder now keeps the last 10 seconds of the fight (the file stays a few MB) and lists the frames each copy replayed (both players need this version)
- Fixed (online): the desync when a knocked-away fighter hits a wall - while someone is knocked away or against a wall, the game now waits for the other player's real input instead of guessing it
- This update compiles one changed game file again
- Fixed: F3 said 'not during online play' in the menus for everyone with the online server set up - it now only refuses during an online battle
- New: press F3 in the game to unlock everything (characters, costumes, skills, stages, music, modes, collections, Galaxy Mode courses); it is kept the next time the game saves. Not during online play
- The debug overlay moved from F3 to F9
- Fixed: a new install could stop with 'Still missing after install: CMake' even though the build tools were there
- Fixed: a ki charge (or other looping) sound could keep playing online after nobody was charging
- Graphics choice: Native 720p, 1080p with AMD FSR (recommended), or 1440p - the Graphics button on the game's page
- Update Hanami first (press F2, 4.6.8 or newer)
- New installs: you need your own Raging Blast 2 AND Raging Blast 1 (USA) Xbox 360 ISOs
- Not in the public beta yet: anime portraits, Android 21, Space Planet (its slot plays Planet)

profiles.name: Native 720p
profiles.desc: The game's own resolution - lightest on your PC, but blurry and jagged on today's screens.

profiles.name: 1080p (FSR)
profiles.desc: Drawn at 720p and upscaled to 1080p with AMD FSR - looks much better and stays light. Recommended.

profiles.name: 1440p
profiles.desc: Drawn at 2560x1440 - the sharpest picture, but very demanding: needs a strong graphics card.
